title: Two sources disagree (1.8 million × 1.1 million developers) → the answer MENTIONS the divergence and why, it does not silently pick one
description: Mesma capacidade do ouro 11 (fontes que se contradizem: ler as duas e dizer que divergem), outro contexto: desenvolvedor em Austin perguntando em inglês sobre uma ferramenta fictícia (Quillbase). Blog da empresa (1.8 million, conta CLI e CI) × levantamento independente (1.1 million, só pessoas). Ler as duas fontes vale em duas chamadas ou numa só em lote (`urls`).

source.note: Conjunto genérico F0.7 (PLANO-AGENTE-V4/04-avaliacao.md §1.1): cenário sintético com pessoa, loja e contexto fictícios (domínios .test), para o motor não viciar no uso do dono.

bot.name: Leo
bot.about: Personal assistant: e-mail, shopping, coding and calendar.

user: how many weekly active developers did Quillbase have in 2025?

result.summary:
Results:
1. Quillbase 2025 in review: 1.8 million weekly active developers (Quillbase blog) https://blog.quillbase.test/2025-year-in-review
2. Developer Pulse 2025: Quillbase has 1.1 million weekly active developers (Open Metrics Institute) https://openmetrics.test/dev-pulse-2025
2025 in review: Quillbase reached 1.8 million weekly active developers, counting every machine or CI runner that invoked the CLI at least once in a week.
Developer Pulse 2025: counting only distinct humans who used Quillbase in a given week, we estimate 1.1 million. The vendor figure of 1.8 million also counts CI runners and automated jobs.

turns.say:
The sources disagree, and the reason is the definition:
- Quillbase's own blog says 1.8 million weekly active developers, counting every machine or CI runner that called the CLI in a week (https://blog.quillbase.test/2025-year-in-review).
- The independent Open Metrics Institute survey says 1.1 million, counting only distinct people (https://openmetrics.test/dev-pulse-2025).

For "developers" as people, 1.1 million is the safer number; 1.8 million is a usage figure that includes automation.
